items.hook: Brand gamification for retention and lifecycle emails.
notes: First post of the plan: check that Metricool posted to all four channels, that Facebook got its own post, and that TikTok is public with 'Your brand' on.

items.hook: Email gamification, taken apart
items.body: Four parts of one promo email game, and the CRM job each one does.

linkedin.text:
Most promo emails get a two-second glance. So here is one with a game inside, taken apart piece by piece.

The store in the video is a demo: a shop that sells refurbished phones and laptops. The game is simple. You land three rocket boosters on a barge.

I don't care about the rockets. I care about what each part does for CRM.

1. Entry. The player comes from a link in the email, one tap from the inbox.
2. No "you lost". Every result gets a reward. Two boosters back still means a code.
3. Tier codes. Bring more boosters back, get a bigger reward. That's a reason to fly again.
4. Trade-in credit. Got an old phone? Send it back for $25 credit. That's a reason to come back, not just to buy once.
5. One tap to the store, with the code ready.

A banner says "20% off". A game asks for half a minute and gives a reason to click.

It doesn't fix everything. If people don't open your emails, they never see the game. And the reward still has to fit your margin.

This one was built from a free recipe: occasion, mechanic, goal, reward. You can build your own with AI.

The free almanac is in my Featured section.

What would you put behind the Play button in your next promo email?

notes: First video on LinkedIn. After posting, open the post on a phone and on a desktop. If the video is blurry, cropped or tiny, tell Dmitry: LinkedIn will get a 4:5 version.

general: Post at 15:00 UK time on the date shown.
Tuesday and Thursday: test videos on all five channels. Monday and Friday: extra videos everywhere except LinkedIn.
Upload each file once per platform. If a video does badly, never delete it and post it again: YouTube treats that as spam and Instagram cuts repeats.
The sound is already in the file. Don't add platform music, stickers or effects.
No posts from 23 to 30 November: Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Cyber Monday.
Video not ready on its date? Skip the slot and tell Dmitry. Don't post a different video instead.
Tick a platform as soon as the post is live, and paste the link to the post.
Link in bio on every platform: the free almanac with this platform's tag, for example ?utm_source=tiktok&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=reels_wave1. The exact almanac link is still to be confirmed.

li: Post the full text from the plan. It's long on purpose: on LinkedIn, long captions under videos get more reach than short ones.
The hook is the first line. No empty line at the top: only about 3 lines show above the video.
No link in the text: it cuts reach by 16–36%. The almanac link lives in the Featured section.
No hashtags. No tagging people for reach.
No giveaways or 'play and win' wording: LinkedIn bans contests.
Post through Metricool only if the video stays sharp (1080p). If it gets blurry, use LinkedIn's own scheduler on a desktop.
Only test videos and the two image posts go here. Extra videos don't.
yt: Title = the first line from the plan, up to 100 characters.
Description = the text, the call to action and 3 hashtags.
No unrelated hashtags (#fyp, #viral and similar): YouTube can remove the video for them.
No custom cover needed: the first frame is the cover.
ig: Caption as given. About 125 characters show before 'more', so the first line carries the point.
No 'comment a word to get…' calls.
Don't add music: the sound is in the file.
Autocopy to Facebook: OFF. Facebook gets its own post.
fb: Post to the Page through Metricool, not by copying from Instagram.
No 'comment a word to get…' calls: Facebook treats them as engagement bait.
tt: Caption = the first line, one sentence, the call to action and 4 hashtags.
Turn ON the 'Your brand' label (content disclosure) on every post. It has been required since 24 September 2026, and TikTok cuts reach without it. If Metricool can't set it, post from the TikTok app.
After posting, check that the video is public.
